Many, many years ago on a hot summer day, I was browsing a book of war poems and came across this:

Wait for me, and I'll come back!
Wait with all you've got!
Wait, when dreary yellow rains
Tell you, you should not.

Wait when snow is falling fast,
Wait when summer's hot,
Wait when yesterdays are past,
Others are forgot.

Wait, when from that far-off place,
Letters don't arrive.
Wait, when those with whom you wait
Doubt if I'm alive.

For some reason that remains a mystery to me, these three stances immediately embedded themselves in my 'remembery'. They keep surfacing at odd times, like a mantra for life. The rest of the poem I forgot. Years later, I couldn't even recall if there was more to it (there was). Curiously, whilst the stanzas remained, the name of the author completely escaped me. It took me many years to rediscover the ID of the poet – Konstantin Simonov. He wrote the poem Wait for me in 1942, from the front to his sweetheart, the actress Valentina Serova.

E-Sports League to Begin Random Drug Testing
I don't know why I didn't think of this before. Of course half of these people or on adderal or ritalin, why wouldn't they be?
In related news: recent e-sports competition only able to field 3 competitors after drug testing became mandatory.

Adderall is about the only 'performance enhancer' that you could even really argue about. Are they going to ban kids with ADHD and a legit prescriptions? If not, whats to stop the other players from getting a shady doc to write them one? I get they want to prevent scandals and protect the brand... but this seems like pissing in the wind.

If someone were taking legit medications that could give them performance enhancing side effects, would it be unfair or wrong to make them sit out? It wouldn't be some sort of punishment for "cheating", but just to try to keep things even.

What about asthmatics who use steroids to allow their lungs to function like they are supposed to... are they out of the competition? Or what about someone who's corrected their vision with surgery? Are glasses an advantage? What about weight class? Is it fair for a 100lb kid to compete against a 300lb kid in these games? If we start down this road... where does it end? Who is it meant to be 'fair' for?

Who is it meant to be 'fair' for?

The competitors.

If the asthmatic's steroids cause increased muscle growth or endurance (which I doubt they would, so this wouldn't get someone disqualified) I don't see how it would be fair for him to compete against other people. The eye surgery/glasses thing doesn't really stand that well. Glasses or eye surgery are intended to give the patient near normal eyesight. Now if someone was going and getting surgery for magical eagle vision, of course it would be a direct advantage and shouldn't be allowed in a competition.

I guess I made my point too subtle. Adderall slows down the brain of an ADHD sufferer to normal levels. If it is okay for someone to correct their vision, why would it not be acceptable to correct a chemical disorder? As for weight class, I'm clearly being facetious, but I could see someone arguing that cardio-pulmonary factors for the two players would not be even and could potentially affect reaction time under stress thus making it "unfair". Should all the competitors eat the same food? Live in the same house? Have the same sleep schedules? Should only clones of the ideal gamer be allowed to compete?

The weight argument is totally null, because muscle bulk doesn't really determine reaction time in any meaningful way. Vision wouldn't really aid you in a game like this. Caffeine consumption maybe? I know I always see the kids chugging Mtn Dew and whatever other terrible soda or energy drink is available. Perhaps that should be limited.

Obviously, I was using hyperbole to make a point about where the line of 'fairness' would be drawn and who it would be drawn for. It's sort of a catch 22 because if they don't effectively discriminate against actual ADHD sufferers, then their tests will just be bypassed with phony prescriptions anyway.
MLB drug tests can be failed by not having drugs in your system. They don't want guys with a script only taking speed on game day to avoid appetite suppression.

Sorry for my absence! I've been away for quite a few weeks now working as an overnight summer camp counselor. Taking on this position this summer brings me to an interesting dilemma I've faced: being vegan at camp. Of course, I don't know how many of you have or have not been to summer camp, but I just thought I'd throw out some tips for those of you in a similar situation.

  1. Let them know! The hardest part of this process for me was making sure all the appropriate people knew about my dietary needs. I know it can be hard to explain to others why this is a need and not a want, but it's worth it in the end. My first week at camp I was eating salads breakfast, lunch, and dinner until I worked up the courage to say something!
  2. Make a list. This one might seem a little tedious, but it's really really helpful in the end. Just making a list of some of your favorite simple vegan dishes, the best protein hearty foods, etc. can really make the conversation easier when it comes to meal planning.
  3. Be prepared. It's important to remember what you're asking for, and with whom. In a position like mine, where I'm an employee, it is my employer's duty to make sure I have enough to eat. However, if you're a guest or a visitor in your location, make sure the expectations are clear.
  4. When in doubt, bring snacks! It's a sad reality that you might not be able to receive ideal meals at camp. Bringing some healthy, satisfying snacks will definitely make the time between meals a little easier and more pleasurable.

I'm sure you guys have some better tips of your own, so please feel free to add them in! Until late August, I will be pretty busy, so my internet presence will be pretty minimal, so please contribute to the subverse. I'd love for this to become more of a community.
